previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and a history of alcohol and benzodiazepine use, was re-admitted after leaving against medical advice the prior day. He presented with hemoptysis and chest pain, and imaging confirmed a pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe with likely infarct and a small to moderate pleural effusion. Despite being hemodynamically stable, he again insisted on leaving the hospital. Due to his prior failure to use prescribed anticoagulation and ongoing substance use, he was not discharged on blood thinners, as it was deemed unsafe. Psychiatry confirmed he had decision-making capacity. He was discharged home on his baseline medications with strong warnings about the life-threatening risk of untreated pulmonary embolism and instructions to seek immediate care if symptoms worsened.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M, hx EtOH abuse, recent PE w/ pulm infarct (s/p AMA 
departure + anticoag noncompliance), s/p frequent falls, ___ 
s/p AICD placement, chronic afib noncompliant on dabigatran, 
HTN, and hx chills/night sweats/cough/thick yellow sputum x 
several months, presented initially with EtOH withdrawal, neck 
and chest pain (found to be ___ C-spine DJD + nerve entrapment), 
dizziness (found to be BPPV), and R foot pain s/p fall (found to 
be ___ previous MVA injuries + EtOH-related neuropathy), 
ultimately also felt to have depression.
.
#. EtOH abuse/withdrawal: Pt reported increased EtOH intake in 3 
days PTA, drinking 1 L rum/day (up from 1 pint/day).  Serum EtOH 
level on admission was 269 (+ pos benzos per tox screen). LFTs 
not suggestive of alcoholic hepatitis. Pt manifested withdrawal 
symptoms including anxiety, tactile and auditory hallucinations 
and was transferred briefly to the ICU, where he was initiated 
on Valium per CIWA scale with adjunct baclofen 10 tid.  Was 
stable for transfer to floor the following day but continued to 
have withdrawal symptoms through HD4.  Patient was continued on 
CIWA protocol during this time.  He was also continued on 
thiamine, folic acid, and MVI.  Pt intially expressed interest 
in quitting and placement at ___, and ___ 
initiated search for placement.  However, placement at rehab was 
deferred pending potential inpatient psych treatment (see 
below). Ultimately patient discharged to ___, and 
was strongly encouraged to pursue outpatient substance abuse 
counseling.
.
# Chest pain: Chronic since ___. Patient had troponin (-) 
x2, non-concerning EKG, non-exertional pattern, and exacerbation 
with palpation. These findings led to low suspicion for 
angina/MI and suggested neuro/MSK etiology, though exacerbation 
from PE could not be ruled out. There was no evidence of 
crepitus on exam, no erythema c/w cellulitis. Lidocaine patches 
started with partial relief. Given hx of fall, CT C-spine 
obtained, which revealed DJD in C4-C7 and particularly narrowing 
of the left C4-C5 foramina. As pt's pain distribution closely 
approximated the cutaneous distribution of recurrent nerves of 
the brachial plexus, his pain was felt to be ___ these neck 
findings. Accordingly, gabapentin 300 qhs was initiated with 
good effect. Pt reported no chest pain at time of discharge.
.
# Pulmonary embolism: Diagnosed ___, but pt left AMA and 
was noncompliant with prescribed Lovenox. Pt expressed 
inconsistent memory of gravity of diagnosis and importance of 
treatment throughout stay, declaring at one point he doubted the 
reality of the diagnosis. TTE revealed no additional R heart 
strain. Pt was restarted on enoxaparin 90 q12h; decision on 
starting warfarin vs. other options was deferred pending 
placement and ability of pt to follow up with outpatient clinics 
given his social situation (homeless, no regular shelter). Pt's 
refusal of all treatments including anticoagulation on HD4 was a 
factor in revealing pt's depression and lack of capacity 
regarding medical decision making, as assessed by Psychiatry on 
___. This prompted legal consult and efforts to secure 
emergency guardianship to ensure continuity of anticoagulation 
treatment during inpatient psychiatric treatment. However, 
patient was again compliant with medications, and Psychiatry on 
___ felt patient did have capacity to make medical decisions.  
During his stay, respiratory status remained stable except for 
one episode of tachypnea felt to be secondary to anxiety.  Given 
concern about patient's prior non-adherence to medications, he 
was ultimately discharged on lovenox ___ mg SC daily for 
long-term anticoagulation of his PE.  Should be on 
anticoagulation at least 6 months.

# Falls/dizziness: Broad differential included BPPV, vasovagal, 
late concussion effects s/p falls (short-term effects including 
bleed were precluded by unremarkable CT head), and EtOH-related 
neuropathy. TTE was reassuring for chronic cardiogenic causes, 
and orthostatics were normal.  Elicitation of specific 
exacerbations with L turning of head, and then L ___, 
made the diagnosis of BPPV. However, simultaneous findings of 
BLE neuropathy and related history of distant injuries s/p MVA 
meant that neuro and MSK etiologies also likely played a role in 
pt's fall frequency. Pt was provided with new cane (previous 
lost/stolen while homeless) to reduce chances of injury, and 
Epley maneuver was demonstrated to patient. By HD7, pt denied 
dizziness as a complaint.  Was noted to be B12 deficient, and 
was started on B12 replacement therapy with injections this 
admission.  Will be discharged on oral replacement therapy.
.
# Cardiomyopathy (EF ___: Known cardiomyopathy reassessed 
due to concern for R heart strain in setting of untreated PE.   
Pt previously prescribed an appropriate regimen including ___, 
beta ___, statin, lasix, but was not compliant with any 
of his meds as outpatient. Once stable on the floor, pt's ___, 
___, and ___ were restarted. He autodiuresed > 1L for 
his first three days on the floor.  Lasix was restarted at 40 mg 
daily, half his outpatient dose. He responded appropriately to 
this regimen and was hemodynamically stable.
.
# Atrial fibrillation: Pt was initially in sinus tachycardia in 
the setting of EtOH withdrawal, but HR improved with appropriate 
CIWA scale dosing of valium. He remained in sinus rhythm, with 
occasional ___ beat runs of non-sustained VT.  He was placed on 
heparin drip in the ICU, which was converted to enoxaparin 90 
q12h upon transfer to the floor. He was hemodynamically stable 
throughout his stay.  Was restarted on metoprolol for rate 
control.
.
# Hypertension, benign: As noted previously, pt was noncompliant 
with all outpatient medications since his last discharge. He was 
restarted on his outpatient doses of metoprolol and losartan 
during this admission. 
.
# RLE pain: Pt presented complaining of R ankle pain radiating 
to knee, with abrasion noted on R knee and tenderness to 
palpation throughout the R foot. X-rays were taken of the ankle 
and knee, which revealed no fracture, dislocation, or other 
acute process. The pt noted previously using a cane, so a cane 
was dispensed and a R ankle brace provided to stabilize the RLE. 
He was inconsistently compliant with the brace, as its initial 
fit caused further abrasion on the RLE; nursing worked to 
prevent abrasion by coordinating with socks/bandages. On HD4, pt 
related prior MVA-associated injury to the RLE, including a 
previous history of leg brace from the ankle to the thigh. As 
pt's chest pain was also thought to have a neuropathic 
component, gabapentin 300 qhs was initiated to control both 
chest and RLE pain, with subsequent improvement in pain.

# Diarrhea: ___ have been secondary to EtOH withdrawal.  Stool 
negative for C. diff.  Diarrhea resolved early in hospital 
course.
.
# Recent history of cough: Pt endorsed a prior history of cough 
with associated production of thick, yellow sputum, chills, and 
night sweats over a several-month period. Given history of 
homelessness w/o shelter and jail time, a high concern for 
tuberculosis was raised. Pt was clear by CXR for active PNA or 
other process. Given high clinical suspicion for latent TB and 
concern for pt's history of leaving AMA, Quantiferon-Gold was 
ordered in preference to PPD. This test returned negative. Pt 
demonstrated no further symptoms of cough or other URI symptoms 
during his stay, and cough was ultimately felt to be secondary 
to resolved CAP.
.
# Depression: On HD4, pt refused medications and expressed 
desire to leave AMA. He was unable to provide a reason for 
leaving, and on further examination, was unable to describe his 
conditions or demonstrate understanding of the risks and 
benefits of deferring treatment. He expressed a belief that his 
conditions were fabricated by the medical staff. He stated that 
he would throw away any medications dispensed for outpatient, 
saying, ""if I die, I die"". Given these findings, psych was 
consulted, who confirmed lack of capacity. Pt was found to be 
severely depressed and passively suicidal; inpatient psychiatric 
treatment was recommended. However, in context of pt's refusing 
medications, concern remained for high risk of medical emergency 
while on inpatient psych if pt continued to refuse medications. 
Therefore, legal was consulted. Given pt's lack of trusted 
family members, petition was begun on HD4 and continued through 
HD7 to secure emergency guardianship to authorize medical 
treatment for anticoagulation and peripheral neuropathy during 
inpatient psychiatry treatment. On HD8, re-evaluation by 
psychiatry found patient to again have capacity with regard to 
his medical treatments; accordingly, emergency guardianship 
search was d/c'd.  Was also felt that patient was no longer 
passively suicidal.  He was strongly encouraged to pursue 
voluntary inpatient psych treatment, but he declined.  He may 
benefit from a partial program, and should have outpatient psych 
follow-up.  ___ also benefit from being restarted on an SSRI.  
Patient discharged to ___, and will follow-up with 
his PCP to determine next steps in outpatient psych treatment. 

The patient had made threats to leave the hospital before

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were hospitalized because you were in withdrawal from 
alcohol, and because you had a clot in your lungs. We gave you 
medicine to help control the shaking, sweating, anxiety, and 
nausea from your withdrawal. We gave you medicine to thin your 
blood (Lovenox) to keep the clot in your lungs from growing. You 
had difficulty keeping food down, so we gave you a bland diet 
and gave you medicine to help with nausea. You had diarrhea, and 
we checked your stool to be sure it was not caused by an 
infection. You expressed interest in quitting alcohol again with 
help from ___, and we spoke to the social 
worker to arrange a place for you to stay. When you expressed 
concern about depression, we also looked for a partial program 
to help you with your mental health.

You also had dizziness with a feeling of the room spinning. We 
examined you and found your dizziness to be caused by crystals 
in your ear that were in the wrong place. We showed you how to 
make the crystals fall into the right place. We also gave you 
medicine to control your dizziness and nausea. We replaced your 
cane to help prevent any more falls.

You fell and hit your head several times before coming to the 
hospital, making your knee and foot hurt. We took X-rays of your 
knee and foot, and did not find any broken bones. We gave you a 
splint to help support your right foot. We also scanned your 
head, and did not find any bleeding near your brain. We scanned 
your neck which did not show broken bones, but you do have 
degenerative changes in the neck, which can explain some of your 
pain. We gave you a pain medicine specific for nerve pain 
(gabapentin), and you felt better.

You told us that you have been coughing for several months. We 
ran tests to try to find if you have an infection. Some of these 
tests have not yet come back from the lab.

You complained of pain around your left shoulder, neck, and 
chest, which has bothered you for several months. We took an EKG 
and scanned your heart with ultrasound, and found that your pain 
was not related to any new heart strain. However, we found that 
you still have heart disease (heart failure) with occassionally 
racing heart (atrial fibrillation) and high blood pressure. We 
gave you medicines to keep your heart rate and blood pressure 
normal, and to avoid worsening of your heart conditions.

We believe the pain in your chest and shoulder may be from 
pinched nerves in your neck from your old car crash injuries. 
Coughing, falling, and the clot in your lungs may also be 
helping to make your pain worse. We gave you a pain medication 
specific for nerve pain (gabapentin), and you felt better.

Because you have been drinking a large amount of alcohol, we 
checked your vitamin levels, and found your vitamin B to be low. 
We gave you vitamins, especially thiamine, folate, and B12, to 
help keep your nerves healthy.

Please follow up with your primary care doctor, ___ at 
___, and as listed below.
